summary: Madrid's municipal rotation car parks are run partly through concessionaires and partly directly by EMT, and the city approves maximum rotational tariffs each year by decree, updated by regional consumer prices. The regional high court annulled the parts of the mobility ordinance defining the citywide low-emission zone in September 2024, the Supreme Court declined to admit the city's appeal in April 2026, and the city council approved a further ordinance modification (Ordinance 2/2026) on 24 March 2026. Metro de Madrid recorded 736.9 million trips in 2025, and the regional transport consortium kept 2026 public transport prices at their second-half 2025 level.

items.text: A May 2021 report says the Supreme Court rejected an appeal by Ecologistas en Acción over the annulment of ordinance articles that underpinned Madrid Central, and that the zone kept issuing fines until that ruling became final. The report adds that the city government planned to replace it with a Madrid 360 scheme.
items.source_title: Así queda Madrid Central hoy tras la anulación del programa

items.text: The Sustainable Mobility Ordinance modification approved in September 2021, which replaced Madrid Central with the broader Madrid 360 low-emission zone set-up, was challenged in the regional high court by Mas Madrid and by Vox in November 2021. The September 2021 amendment date is also cited in the city's own 2025 car park tariff decree.
items.source_title: Más Madrid y Vox recurren la Ordenanza de Movilidad aprobada por Almeida que eliminó Madrid Central

items.text: A January 2022 article described a dynamic tariff for regulated on-street parking (SER) that raises meter prices by 60 percent when nitrogen dioxide readings exceed 60 micrograms per cubic metre and doubles them above 70. It reports zero-emission vehicles exempt and ECO-label vehicles discounted by up to 75 percent.
items.source_title: Llega la tarifa dinámica del SER: parquímetros más caros los días de alta contaminación

items.text: A report published on 17 September 2024 says the regional high court (TSJM) annulled the parts of the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance that defined the scope of the citywide low-emission zone, after a challenge by Vox, because the prior reports, especially the economic one, were insufficient. The ruling was not yet final and the city could still file a cassation appeal.
items.source_title: Golpe a Madrid, la justicia echa abajo su Zona de Bajas Emisiones tras el recurso presentado por VOX

items.text: A report of 22 April 2026 says the Supreme Court refused to admit the city's appeal against the September 2024 TSJM annulment, leaving that ruling final, and that the annulled rules had already been replaced by a newer ordinance. The report adds that Vox announced a motion for the 29 April municipal plenary asking the mayor to refund low-emission-zone fines.
items.source_title: El Tribunal Supremo cierra la batalla legal de las ZBE de Madrid, pero nada cambia para los conductores

items.text: The Madrid city council plenary approved Ordinance 2/2026 on 24 March 2026, amending the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance on special-protection low-emission zones and regulated on-street parking (SER); corrections to its text were published in the regional gazette in May 2026.
items.source_title: Corrección de los errores materiales advertidos en el texto de la Ordenanza 2/2026, de 24 de marzo, por la que se modifica la Ordenanza de Movilidad Sostenible, de 5 de octubre de 2018, en materia de zonas de bajas emisiones de especial protección y del servicio de estacionamiento regulado y de los errores materiales de edición informática advertidos en el texto publicado de la ordenanza en el BOAM n.º 10.103, de 10 de abril de 2026

items.text: A report of 11 December 2025 says a draft change to the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance, due for initial approval by the city government that day, would let regulated on-street parking (SER) spread in phases to up to 22 more neighbourhoods: about 11,372 spaces by the end of 2029, then a second phase to 2035 adding 66,120 spaces, reaching Puente de Vallecas and Moratalaz for the first time. It would also allow extended SER hours beyond 21:00 on weekdays, from 15:00 on Saturdays and on Sundays and holidays in high-demand zones.
items.source_title: Los parquímetros podrán extenderse por 22 barrios más de Madrid con la nueva Ordenanza de Movilidad

items.text: The city's 2025 tariff decree sets park-and-ride (disuasorio) use at EMT car parks as free if the car stays between 5 and 16 hours and the user also uses public transport during the stay; otherwise the general rotational tariff applies.
items.source_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.text: In October 2020 the regional transport consortium announced plans to add 19 car parks to its Aparca+T park-and-ride network, including three EMT car parks in Madrid city (Wanda Metropolitano, Nuestra Señora del Recuerdo and Avenida de Portugal). This was a plan, not a completed rollout.
items.source_title: La Comunidad de Madrid prepara la incorporación de 19 aparcamientos a la red de parkings disuasorios Aparca+T

items.text: The decree sets 2025 maximum rotational tariffs for cars, VAT included, in both directly managed (EMT) and concession car parks: 0.0496 euros per minute for 0-30 minutes, 0.0448 for 31-90 and 0.0594 for 91-660 minutes, and 38.00 euros for 661 minutes up to 24 hours. It cites a 1.5 percent change in the regional consumer price index between September 2023 and September 2024.
items.source_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.text: The decree, effective 1 January 2025, sets a high-demand tariff 30 percent above the generic one for the first four hours at rotation car parks less than 400 metres from venues able to hold over 5,000 people during large events, starting one hour before the event, with a 15 percent reduction for vehicles with three or more occupants. Applying the tariff and the reduction requires the car park operator to have technology to verify actual occupancy.
items.source_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.text: The city's tariff decree states that the municipal car park service is provided both through concessionaires and through direct management by EMT, the wholly city-owned transport company. It also lets EMT apply tariffs that take a vehicle's environmental label into account in its directly managed car parks.
items.source_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.text: On 27 July 2023 the city government approved the tender for a roughly 25-year concession for three Calle Velázquez car parks (Ayala, Jorge Juan, Juan Bravo), with residents' use rights respected until 1 June 2048. The report gives 1,894 spaces, including 622 for residents and 128 reserved for electric charging, and says the concessionaire must spend about 17.2 million euros on modernisation.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento de Madrid privatiza hasta el 2048 tres parkings de la calle Velázquez que ingresan 4,1 millones al año

items.text: EMT Madrid's 2025 accounts, reported in March 2026, show 19.2 million euros of income from its car parks.
items.source_title: Cuentas 2025 cierran con beneficio de 3,26 millones y récords de viajes

items.text: A report of 14 February 2024 says EMT had completed upgrades at four public car parks (Pedro Zerolo, Plaza Mayor, Olavide and Almagro) that added 14 charge points in total. It adds that municipal plans cover 33 new chargers across ten car parks, including those four, funded by EU Next Generation money.
items.source_title: Localizamos los 14 puntos de recarga en aparcamientos públicos que estrena Madrid

items.text: In mid-2020 the city had 45 public fast-charging points (31 on public land, 14 on private property), and EMT had signed an agreement with i-DE covering charge points in EMT-managed car parks and public spaces.
items.source_title: Madrid moderniza la red pública de recarga rápida

items.text: The national open data catalogue datos.gob.es lists an Ayuntamiento de Madrid dataset, 'EMT. Aparcamientos EMT', describing the location and characteristics of EMT-run municipal car parks (rotation, resident, mixed and park-and-ride); the dataset was created on 4 November 2025 and its file distributions are dated 14 February 2026.
items.source_title: EMT. Aparcamientos EMT

items.text: The city's open data portal lists an EMT dataset of total and available spaces per car park by hour (CSV, update frequency daily) alongside a customer satisfaction study on EMT car parks updated in July 2026.
items.source_title: Conjunto de datos - Portal de datos abiertos del Ayuntamiento de Madrid (listing filtered by keyword 'emt')

items.text: The Community of Madrid reported on 16 January 2026 a record 736,874,012 Metro de Madrid trips in 2025, 3 percent above the 715,208,882 of 2024. It says the busiest day in the company's history, excluding 12 March 2004, was 28 November (Black Friday) with 2,819,020 trips.
items.source_title: La Comunidad de Madrid alcanza en 2025 el récord histórico de usuarios de Metro con un total de 736.874.012

items.text: The regional transport consortium resolved on 29 December 2025 to keep 2026 public transport prices at their second-half 2025 level, under a national decree-law providing fare subsidies (free child passes, 50 percent off youth passes, 20 percent off other multi-trip passes).
items.source_title: RESOLUCIÓN de 29 de diciembre de 2025, de la Dirección-Gerencia del Consorcio Regional de Transportes Públicos Regulares de Madrid, por la que se dispone la publicación del acuerdo del Consejo de Administración por el que se determinan los precios del transporte público en el año 2026

items.text: Madrid's tourism yearbook reports record international tourist spending in 2025 of 17.9 billion euros (71 percent above 2019) and more than 11 million visitors, and says the city now exceeds 900,000 visitors a month for nine months of the year.
items.source_title: Madrid 2025 Anuario Turismo
